**Disk-persistent autotune cache**: `~/.cache/kiln/autotune/{backend}-{device_uuid}.json`, keyed on `{shape, dtype, layout, concurrent_streams, kiln_version}`. Applies to cublasLt heuristics, MPS tile selection, and Vulkan workgroup-size search uniformly. Cold-start never re-tunes a known shape. **`concurrent_streams` matters**: the optimal algo for a matmul running solo on the device is *not* the optimal algo when two other QKV matmuls are running on parallel streams competing for SMs. Cache key includes the planner's `expected_concurrent_streams` so Phase 3's parallel-QKV picks SM-light algos automatically.

**Pre-shipped autotune cache (Qwen3.5-4B specialization).** Ship `assets/autotune/{backend}-{gpu_sku}.json` *in the binary* for the tier-1 GPU list (RTX 4060 Ti / 4070 Laptop / 4090 / RTX 6000 Ada / A6000 / L40S / A100 80 GB / H100). Cold-start on tier-1 hardware has zero tune cost — the user's first decode token is at steady-state speed. Unknown GPUs fall back to the runtime heuristic and write back to the local cache (existing path); the upstream PR adds the new SKU to the shipped set. **The win is asymmetric**: cublasLt heuristic search is 50-200 ms per shape; Qwen3.5-4B has ~20 distinct GEMM shapes; that is 1-4 s of cold-start time eliminated on tier-1 hardware.

For pure-inference Parameters (no `backward_storage`), forward_storage is canonical. **Eval-while-training via Parameter snapshot.** Eval acquires `Parameter::snapshot(epoch)` at job start; training continues to mutate the master; the snapshot is refcounted and the storage isn't freed until eval completes. On 16 GiB this is opt-in (snapshot doubles weight VRAM); on 48 GiB+ default-on. Eliminates the "training pauses for eval" delay that `eval/mod.rs:1-7` inherits today from the write-lock.

With concurrent serve+train, the trainer can generate rollouts from the *current* policy by issuing forward-only requests through the same scheduler, snapshot the policy at rollout start, update from the rollouts, repeat. The GRPO outer loop tightens from minutes/step to seconds/step. This is a defining capability of the Kiln pitch.

**kiln-tensor allocator "freeze-pointers" mode.** Active for the duration of `capture()` … `replay()`. Allocations during freeze come from a pre-sized pool with no reclamation. This is the structural fix that makes batched cuda-graph capture possible; without it Phase 8 doesn't land. On CUDA, "freeze" enables `cudaMallocFromPoolAsync` capture-mode and the driver tracks pointer lifetimes natively (CUDA 12.0+); the kiln-side audit is a defense-in-depth, not the primary mechanism.

**Capture-lifetime programming model (the dangling-pointer rule).** Any tensor whose `.device_ptr()` enters a captured graph must outlive every replay of that graph. Lifetimes are encoded in the type system where possible (`CapturedGraph<'a>` borrows from a `FrozenAllocator<'a>`) and enforced by a debug-assertion `kiln_tensor::audit_captured_pointers()` that walks the graph and verifies every recorded pointer still resolves to a live allocation. A failing audit is a graph-invalidation, not a silent corruption.

**8.1 Persistent attention kernel.** One CUDA kernel runs many decode steps without re-launch, reading paged-KV slot indices from a device-side queue updated by the scheduler. Targets the per-launch overhead floor (~3-5 µs × num_layers × decode_steps). Reference shape: FlashInfer's persistent-attn, lifted to the kiln-tensor + paged-KV interface. Expected win: 1.1-1.3× on bs=1, fades at bs=64 where launch overhead amortizes.

**8.2 Persistent / megakernel MLP.** Single fused kernel doing gate+up+silu+down across an entire layer (or block of layers) without intermediate global-memory roundtrips. Requires careful register/shmem budgeting; only viable on H100+ with enough resources. Expected win: ~10% decode tok/s when combined with 8.1.

**8.3 On-device stop-condition prefix match.** Today: GPU samples → 1 u32 D2H → CPU stop-sequence check → next iter (`generate.rs:1556-1670`, `:3041`). The D2H sync is the inherent decode-latency floor. Move stop-sequence prefix match on-device for greedy decode; CPU only sees a 1-bit "should_stop" signal per request. Eliminates the last sync point in the bs=1 decode hot loop.

**8.4 FP8 forward training (Hopper / Blackwell).** FP32 master + FP8 activation/gradient scaling, per-tensor or per-block. The `Parameter` type from Phase 2.5 already accommodates (`forward_storage = FP8`, `backward_storage = FP32` or `BF16` master). The work is the scaling-factor pipeline (forward saves max-abs per tensor; backward applies inverse scale) and the cublasLt FP8 GEMM path. Biggest training perf lever on H100+; not in scope for candle-removal but the substrate makes it cheap to add.

**8.5 cuda-mempool-captured graph at variable bs.** Once allocator sits over `cudaMemPool_t` (Phase 1), capture a *single* graph parameterized by bs and let the driver pick the mempool block per replay. Reduces VRAM cost of the bs∈{1..64} graph family from 7× to ~1.5× scratch.

**8.6 L2 cache persistence (`cudaAccessPolicyWindow`).** Lock hot small tensors — RoPE cos/sin tables, RMSNorm scale parameters, GDN A/B recurrent matrices, the active LoRA delta — into the L2 cache. Especially impactful on consumer 4090-class cards with smaller L2 (72 MB) where global-memory traffic dominates over compute. Expected: 5–15 % decode tok/s on bs=1. Per-tier cost: zero VRAM; consumes ~0.5 % of L2 per tensor. Per-tier impact: largest on 16–24 GiB tier (smallest L2 relative to working set); smaller on 80 GiB H100 (L2 already covers more of the working set).

**8.7 CUDA Graph conditional nodes (CUDA 12.4+).** Phase 5's 7-graph family (bs∈{1,2,4,8,16,32,64}) sizes at 80 GiB; on 16 GiB it auto-downsamples and the family becomes coarse. Conditional nodes collapse the family to **one** graph parameterized at replay time, reducing graph-capture VRAM from 7× scratch to 1× scratch and making the bs sweep continuous, not stepped. Replaces the manual key-by-bs lookup in `cuda_graph.rs`. Direct enabler of the 16 GiB tier hitting the full bs sweep.

**8.8 Hopper cluster launch + DSM for GDN recurrence.** GDN recurrent state crosses CTA boundaries today (one thread block per row, sync via global memory). On SM≥90, `__cluster_dims_t` + distributed shared memory lets neighbor CTAs cooperate without a global-memory roundtrip. Expected: 10–20 % on the GDN-dominant decode path (PROFILING.md records `kiln/gdn/in_proj` at 19.6 % of forward). Hopper-only; fall-through uses today's kernel.

**8.9 2:4 structured sparsity for the LoRA-frozen base.** Marlin-frozen base weights become candidates for 2:4-sparse re-pack during model load (one-shot offline cost). NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores deliver 2× FLOPS on A100/H100/RTX 6000 Ada for 2:4-sparse matmuls. LoRA delta stays dense (rank-`r` matmul is too small to benefit). Per-tier: largest win on 16–48 GiB where weights are bandwidth-bound. Small accuracy drop (literature: <0.5 %) compensated by the active LoRA adapter.

**8.10 NVFP4 / MXFP6 forward (Blackwell).** Phase 1's DType enum lists `FP4Packed`; this item ships the MX-format scaling pipeline — per-block (32-element) FP4 storage with FP8 scales, native Blackwell tensor-core ingestion. Per-tier: **4× memory reduction** (2 GiB Marlin → 1 GiB MXFP4) makes Qwen3.5-4B fit on 8 GiB cards for inference and unlocks bigger context everywhere. Backward stays in BF16 master (Phase 2.5 contract).

**8.11 Programmatic Dependent Launch (PDL).** CUDA 12.0+: kernel B can start on the SM as soon as kernel A finishes its prologue (not its full body), overlapping launch latency with prior-kernel epilogue. Especially impactful for the many-small-kernel decode path (RMSNorm → matmul → residual → norm → …). Expected: 5–10 % on bs=1 where launch overhead is a measurable fraction of step time.

**8.12 FlashAttention-3 path (Hopper/Blackwell, CUDA).** Today `kiln-flash-attn` uses cutlass FA2-style kernels. FA3 adds warp-specialized async (producer/consumer split of TMA loads vs WGMMA math) plus a persistent-tile schedule that hides prologue/epilogue under math. Expected: ~1.5–2× over FA2 on H100 at the long-seq prefill shapes Qwen3.5-4B hits at 32K-128K context. Phase 5's "persistent attention" line gets its concrete kernel here. Per-tier: Hopper-only win at first; fall-through is the existing FA2 path. Reads/writes through paged-KV via the Phase 3 slot-tensor seam (preserved byte-for-byte).

**8.13 KV cache compression beyond FP8 (KIVI int4 + ScissorHands/H2O eviction).** FP8 K/V (Phase 3) gives 2× over BF16; KIVI gives another 2× (int4 K, FP8 V with per-channel quantization) on top. ScissorHands/H2O are *eviction* policies — drop low-attention-score KV slots from cache, recompute on demand. For Qwen3.5-4B at 128K context, the KV cache currently dominates VRAM on every tier; this halves it again. Per-tier: largest absolute win on 16–24 GiB where context length is the binding constraint. Composes with `PagedKvCache::new_with_fp8` (Phase 3) as a third storage variant; the slot-tensor interface stays the same. Accuracy bound: KIVI literature reports <0.5% perplexity delta; gate with a Qwen3.5-4B eval-suite parity check.

**8.14 GPUDirect Storage / kvikIO async weight load.** Cold-start Qwen3.5-4B BF16 weight load is ~3-8 s today via `memmap2` + `spawn_blocking` (`crates/kiln-model/src/weights.rs`). GDS / kvikIO does NVMe-to-VRAM DMA bypassing the CPU/page-cache hop. Per-tier: most visible on 16-48 GiB tier where the user's iteration loop is "load → bench → tweak → reload"; less visible on 80 GiB where the server is long-running. Composes with the on-disk transposed-weight cache (`transposed_weight_cache.rs`) — both bypass the page cache. Falls through to the existing mmap path where the kernel/driver doesn't support GDS.

**8.15 NVRTC runtime kernel fusion for shape-tail epilogues.** cublasLt epilogues are a fixed menu (bias, activation, gelu, ...); shape-dependent fused tails (e.g., "matmul + RMSNorm + residual + RoPE" specialized to Qwen3.5-4B's exact head-dim and rope-base) are not in the menu. `kiln-codegen` is a runtime kernel-source builder that emits PTX via NVRTC, keyed on the same `{shape, dtype, layout}` tuple as the autotune cache; on Vulkan/Metal the equivalent is SPIR-V / MSL generation through the existing pipeline cache. Once written, the cached kernel persists with the autotune cache (Phase 2 pre-shipped variant). The point is to chase fusions cublasLt structurally cannot do for us, not to reinvent cublasLt.

**8.17 Hand-shaped persistent megakernel for Qwen3.5-4B's exact dim quadruple (specialization of 8.2).** The persistent MLP megakernel in 8.2 is parameterized — re-spell it for Qwen3.5-4B's (2560, 18432, 18432, 2560) gate/up/down dims as a single hand-tuned kernel. Register budget, shmem tiling, and warp-specialization schedule are baked against the known shape. Composes with 8.10 (NVFP4) and 8.11 (PDL); supersedes the parameterized 8.2 variant on tier-1 hardware. The kernel zoo grows by one file; the perf delta is the part 8.2's parameterization left on the table.

**8.18 GPU-side BPE tokenizer for the Qwen3.5-4B vocabulary.** Specialized to vocab=152064 and the fixed merge table. Eliminates host tokenization on very-long prompts (today the prefill upload includes a CPU-side BPE pass that scales with prompt bytes). Per-tier: matters most when a server fields long-context requests at high QPS. Read-only kernel — emits token ids directly into the pinned upload buffer.

**8.19 Closed-loop GPU decode for greedy.** Combine Phase 4's on-device stop-condition (already promoted to Phase 4 gate as item 8.3) with Phase 8.1 persistent attention into a single megakernel that loops N decode steps internally — D2H is a 1-bit "should_stop" signal per request per N iterations. The bs=1 hot loop becomes "launch megakernel → poll 1 bit." This is the inherent decode-latency floor on greedy — the absolute minimum Qwen3.5-4B can take per token on a given GPU. Per-tier: largest absolute win on consumer 16-24 GiB cards where launch overhead is a measurable fraction of step time; small relative win on H100 where compute already saturates.

**`KILN_DETECT_ANOMALY` NaN/Inf trap wired through the autograd tape.** Off by default (cost is ~5% per step); on under the training parity tests in CI. Every backward op asserts `is_finite()` on its output and panics with the op's tape position on first violation. Today the only finiteness check is `kiln-train`'s reward-stats receipt warning *after* the step. With the trap, training corruption surfaces at the kernel that produced the first non-finite value, not 100 steps later when loss diverges. Composes with the in-place tape invariant (anti-pattern 16) — both are tape-position-aware safety nets.

**`KILN_DETERMINISTIC=1` envelope.** Single flag forcing the deterministic codepath for every "deterministic by construction" item from Phase 0's determinism stance: `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`, the deterministic-atomicAdd embedding bwd variant, the deterministic reduction-tree softmax/RMSNorm bwd, the warp-shuffle-free reduction in cross-entropy bwd. Each backend supplies the deterministic variant of any op flagged "tolerance-bounded" in Phase 0. CI runs training parity tests under the envelope and validates bit-reproducibility across two runs at the same seed. The flag is the user-facing contract for RL / SFT iteration reproducibility — "I want this run to match yesterday's run" becomes one env var, not a doc-read.
